title: Check-in and welcome light breakfast
abstract: Badge check-in with coffee and a light breakfast before the opening.

title: Opening / Welcome session
Keynote
Web-less Console: Standalone Apps in Symfony 8.2
abstract: Symfony 8.2 gives the Console component a DI-powered foundation with no HTTP layer, so standalone CLI tools get a real container and service wiring as first-class framework citizens.

title: Why AI Output Is the New XSS
abstract: Treating LLM output as trusted input opens the door to XSS and injection (OWASP LLM05). Learn to sanitize model output, render Markdown safely and stay professionally pessimistic about AI content.

title: Pedal to the Metal: Compiling PHP to Native Code
abstract: A tour of Elephc, a Rust-written compiler that turns a static subset of PHP into native machine code, from an everyday example to a Doom-style demo, limits included.

title: Break
abstract: Coffee break, sponsored by Ibexa.

title: Beyond the Demo: Shipping Real AI Features
abstract: Patterns for running Symfony AI features in production: human-in-the-loop approval, long-running workflows, retries, cost tracking and the extension points you need once the happy path ends.

title: Symfony UX + Symfony AI: Taking Agent Interactions to the Next Level
abstract: Combining Symfony UX and Symfony AI so agents interact through maps, charts and autocompletes and update the UI live with Turbo, using a small PHP implementation of the AG-UI protocol.

title: Beyond Mocks
abstract: Modern ways to test HTTP integrations with Symfony HttpClient: controlling responses, recording and replaying real traffic, and checking API contracts, instead of piling up fragile mocks.

title: Your Parents Holidayed in Yugoslavia
abstract: How a hobby flight logger outgrew CRUD: event sourcing with just Symfony, Doctrine and Messenger, with append-only events, projections and temporal queries over messy aviation data.

title: Exposing Your API to AI Agents
abstract: After an MCP refresher, compares ways to give agents tools with Symfony and API Platform: generated tools, a Hydra hypermedia gateway, or attribute-declared tools, built live and weighed honestly.

title: Giving AI Agents a Durable Memory
abstract: Using user- and project-level instructions to route agents through a small, versioned Markdown knowledge base so they keep context across sessions, and where native memory or retrieval fits better.

title: Lunch
final class Entity: Doctrine Mapping for Modern PHP
abstract: Modern PHP features let Doctrine ORM 3.4 and DBAL 4.3 drop old workarounds. A realistic entity is refactored live into final classes with enums, typed IDs and value objects, with no schema change.

title: The Hidden Cost of `return new Response()`
abstract: Why buffering whole responses hurts, and how to stream instead with StreamedResponse, JsonStreamer, iterable Doctrine sources and Server-Sent Events to keep memory flat and time-to-first-byte low.

title: Form Component Through the Ages: History of (not so) Black Magic
abstract: Fifteen years of the Form component explained: type extensions, transformers, form events, 7.4 multi-step forms and the new 8.2 attribute-based forms, so its magic becomes readable.

title: PHP Wasn't Supposed to Do That
abstract: Symfony UX Native turns one Symfony codebase into real iOS and Android apps via Hotwire Native, with a live bridge component and an honest look at limits and good use cases.

title: From Serializer to JsonStreamer: the debrief
abstract: A team whose Elasticsearch reindexing took hours replaced custom Serializer normalizers with Symfony JsonStreamer; an honest report on the challenges and what was learned.

title: When vibes meets reality
abstract: Bringing testing, architecture and engineering rigour to low-code and vibe-coding platforms that non-developers use to ship tools to production, following one function from idea to release.

title: Green Is Not Done
abstract: When agents write code, CI becomes their definition of done. Harness engineering for existing Symfony apps: PHPStan and deptrac as agent feedback, custom architecture rules and a baseline ratchet.

title: Securing Your API: The OWASP API Top 10
abstract: A walk through the OWASP API Security Top 10, from broken authorization to injection, with ways to prevent each flaw in the APIs behind modern applications.

title: Real Browsers, Real Kernel: Playwright Testing in Symfony
abstract: PlaywrightPHP and a Symfony bundle let real-browser tests run against the test kernel in the same PHP process, asserting on DOM, events and database state together, with three live demos.

title: Break
abstract: Coffee break, sponsored by Ibexa.

title: Composer & Packagist Supply Chain Security: Report from the trenches
abstract: How Composer and Packagist responded to supply chain attacks: malware detection, a transparency log, dependency policies, immutable releases and minimum release age, plus tips and the 2027 outlook.

title: Core Team Q/A
abstract: Open questions to the Symfony Core Team.

title: Community Evening
abstract: Evening party at NINE'S, Robert Lewandowski's sports bar near the venue, with drinks and finger food. Badge required.

title: Light breakfast
Ten Easy Steps Towards a More Inclusive Workplace
abstract: Ten everyday situations where small changes in language and behaviour, and awareness of implicit bias, make a team or company more inclusive, with practical examples.

title: Mercure 1.0: Real-Time Symfony, Eight Years On
abstract: Mercure 1.0 ships with a new Symfony integration, URL Pattern and OAuth Rich Authorization Requests support and optional OIDC compatibility, for real-time features and streaming AI output.

title: Developing the Developer: A Year of Journaling with AI
abstract: An open-sourced, IDE-based journaling system built with LLMs for tracking growth as a developer, and what a year of use taught about writing, MCP data sources and pitfalls.

title: Works on my machine. The agent said so.
abstract: Lessons from running coding agents across a team at Upsun: sandboxing untrusted code, keeping models deterministic, shared context over personal prompt files, and judging work beyond passing tests.

title: Break
abstract: Coffee break, sponsored by Ibexa.

title: Fixing PHP2Shell
abstract: The full story of the PHP2Shell vulnerability: discovery through agentic security research, validation, the coordinated fix by the PHP team, and lessons for the ecosystem.

title: Protect Your Data with Queryable Encryption
abstract: Client-side field encryption with Doctrine and a key management system, covering algorithms and key rotation, so sensitive data stays unreadable to the database yet remains queryable.

title: If You Build It, They Won't Come
abstract: Four questions to ask before building a feature, how to kill weak ideas with evidence, and why the same answers become the positioning you need to get people to use it.

title: Headless vs Monolith: The Final Battle
abstract: Headless versus monolith compared for Symfony e-commerce, and the hybrid middle ground with Symfony UX, Live and Twig Components, drawn from experience at Sylius.

title: Symfony Mate: From Hallway Idea to Daily Driver
abstract: Mate gives coding agents insight into a running Symfony app. It swapped its MCP server for a native CLI after measuring agent tool use, and agent skills now ship with packages. Live demo.

title: The building blocks of an agentic software factory
abstract: A conceptual map of an agentic software factory around the coding agent: intent and specs, verification, delivery and operations, and strategy, linked by shared context and human decisions.

title: Lunch
Calling the Symfony Container from Legacy Code
abstract: Booting the Symfony container from legacy PHP so both sides of a migration share services with full dependency injection, with trade-offs and sharp edges spelled out.

title: Beyond HTML: Colocating Assets in Twig Components
abstract: Keeping each Twig component's CSS, JavaScript and images next to its template, demonstrated with the open-source AtomicAssetsBundle, and the trade-offs of component-scoped assets.

title: From 30% to 100%: Fifteen Years of Hearing Loss and Tech
abstract: A personal look at six technologies that transformed a deaf engineer's career, why accessibility helps everyone, and three concrete actions developers can take to build more inclusive tech.

title: From 14s to 1.8s: A Symfony Cold Start Autopsy
abstract: Hunting down a 14-second Cloud Run cold start: the tooling, framework internals and misleading optimizations involving image size, autoloading, the compiled container and cache warmup.

title: You Are (Not) a Machine
abstract: A mostly non-technical, mental-health talk comparing the HttpKernel's event listeners with the legacy behavioural listeners we learned early in life that may hold us back today.

title: Zero to production on SymfonyCloud, live
abstract: Live on stage: build a small Symfony app, deploy it to SymfonyCloud without build scripts, then find a bottleneck with Blackfire and move work to a background worker.

title: PHP’s Type System Dissected
abstract: What a type system formally is, how PHP's grew, how LSP and variance govern subtyping, where it is sound or compromised, and what could come next, now that types also guide AI models.

title: Not All Messenger Transports Are Equal
abstract: A data-driven comparison of Symfony Messenger transports: retries, idempotency, acknowledgement, behaviour under load and failure, and cost, to help choose the right queue.

title: Nobody typed this: reviewing agentic code
abstract: A review policy for agent-written pull requests: who reviews, what to check, how much review a change needs, who stays accountable, and how to record why a change was made.

title: Break
abstract: Coffee break, sponsored by Ibexa.

title: Sponsor Prizes
The PHP Runtime I Want to See
abstract: Adding background workers to FrankenPHP: long-running PHP outside HTTP that publishes data requests read directly, with no serialization, TTL or restart, and no changes to controllers.

title: Closing session
Hackday
abstract: Free contributor day at a separate venue (Tadeusza Czackiego 15/17): bring a laptop for onboarding, mentoring and work on Symfony. Sponsored by Baksla.sh.
